rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Biology is the scientific study of living organisms, from molecules (DNA, proteins) to the entire biosphere. It encompasses branches such as Botany, Zoology, Microbiology, Genetics, Ecology, Physiology, Anatomy, Taxonomy, and Biotechnology. Living things share seven characteristics: cellular organisation, metabolism, homeostasis, growth, reproduction, response to stimuli, and evolution.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Biology = Bios (life) + Logos (study) = the study of living organisms
Scope: molecule → cell → tissue → organ → organism → population → community → ecosystem → biosphere
Scientific method: Observation → Question → Hypothesis → Experiment → Data → Conclusion

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Biology is NOT the same as medicine or agriculture; it is the foundational science, and medicine/agriculture are applied fields.  ·  Botany studies plants (including algae and fungi in some systems); Zoology studies animals.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects the definition of biology, the 9-level scope, and the 7 characteristics of life.  ·  The scientific method is a favourite exam question (6 steps).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Botany: Oryza sativa (rice) — a monocot, angiosperm, Poaceae.  ·  Zoology: Rana tigrina (tiger frog) — an amphibian, Chordata, Anura.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Microbiology includes bacteria, viruses, fungi, protists; it overlaps with botany and zoology.  ·  Physiology = function; Anatomy = structure; they are complementary, not the same.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Biology: the study of living organisms.  ·  Scope: from molecules to the biosphere (9 levels).  ·  Branches: Botany, Zoology, Microbiology, Genetics, Ecology, Physiology, Anatomy, Taxonomy, Biotechnology.  ·  Characteristics of life: cellular, metabolism, homeostasis, growth, reproduction, response, evolution.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: There are approximately 8.7 million species on Earth (only ~15% described).  ·  Biology is the fastest-growing science; over 200,000 biology research papers are published annually.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Explain the scientific method (steps).  ·  Differentiate botany from zoology (4 points).  ·  Describe the key features of Scope and Fields of Biology.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Differentiate botany from zoology.  ·  Scope and Fields of Biology is frequently tested.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Microbiology: Escherichia coli — a Gram-negative, prokaryotic bacterium.  ·  Genetics: Mendel's pea experiments — the foundation of modern genetics.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Biology is the study of: → B  ·  The branch of biology that studies plants is: → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Biology: the study of living organisms (Greek: bios = life, logos = study).  ·  Scope: from molecules (DNA, proteins) to cells, tissues, organs, organisms, populations, communities, ecosystems, and the biosphere.  ·  Branches: Botany (plants), Zoology (animals), Microbiology (microorganisms), Genetics (heredity), Ecology (organism-environment), Physiology (function), Anatomy (structure), Taxonomy (classification), Biotechnology (application).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Species diversity  ·  5 Scopes of Biology Biology is very important as it helps us to understand nature and living things and adjust to our surroundings.  ·  Its application extends far beyond basic scientific research, impacting crucial sectors like health, genetics, nursing, agriculture, environmental science, and conservation.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The diverse scopes of biology underscore its importance in addressing societal challenges and advancing technological innovations that benefit both humans and the environment.  ·  Some important scopes of biology can be discussed under following heads: 1.  ·  In the Field of Health, Disease and Medicine: Biology provides essential knowledge for understanding human health, disease mechanisms, and developing medical treatments.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Scientific method: observation → hypothesis → experiment → conclusion.  ·  Biology is an experimental, evidence-based science.  ·  ~8.7 million species; only ~15% described.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: A "characteristic of life" must be present in ALL living things (e.g., metabolism, reproduction); not all organisms reproduce sexually (some reproduce asexually).  ·  The scientific method is iterative; a single experiment rarely proves a hypothesis.  ·  Distinguish between key concepts in Scope and Fields of Biology.
